item.title: Going after ghosts: Ghost Jobs and the Broken Economic Map
item.description:
Lawmakers are targeting ghost jobs...
Good morning, and many happy returns to the world’s oldest living person, Ethel Caterham, who turned 117 yesterday. Caterham once attributed her longevity to her agreeable demeanor, telling the Associated Press, her secret was “never arguing with anyone.” It’s way too late for us to try that, so I guess we’ll have to stick with eating right and getting enough sleep for long enough that Bryan Johnson figures out how to make us immortal.

item.title: Your best shot: Our digital future hits a physical wall
item.description:
A cancer vaccine had success in trials...
Hold our spot. Not content to simply spend their weekends waiting in lines for pastries that have gone viral on TikTok, New Yorkers are now bringing that energy to a less trendy pastime: buying movie tickets. Business Insider reports that the line at one Manhattan cinema to snag tickets to see Dune: Part 3 in 70-millimeter IMAX format when it opens in December stretched 1,500 feet. They’re one enormous bed sheet away from honoring Shai Hulud with an epic group costume.

item.title: Coming to court: Trillion dollar lawsuits and viral cartoon cows
item.description:
Meta faces a trillion-dollar lawsuit...
Salutations. Bank CEOs—they’re just like us! Ever played a fun little game with your coworkers where you have to sneak words into a presentation (or, erm, into your newsletter as Word of the Day)? Well, according to the Wall Street Journal, Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan sure has . That’s apparently why he tosses off SAT words like “gainsay,” “fantods,” and “anfractuous” during quarterly earnings calls with analysts. The head of America’s second-largest bank typically uses at least one ten-dollar word per call, and one BofA insider told the WSJ that the unusual words Moynihan slips into prepared scripts are randomly chosen just before the calls start.
https://www.morningbrew.com/issues/coming-to-court

item.title: Major shift: Why students are ditching computer science
item.description:
AI is changing how students pick college majors...
Good morning, and congratulations to Jinny Lu, the winner of the 50th annual World’s Ugliest Dog Contest. In case you need to turn this moment into a LinkedIn post, here’s what the pug with its tongue hanging out of the side of its mouth taught us about perseverance. Jinny Lu’s path to winning the $5,000 prize and eternal bragging rights wasn’t easy: Before being adopted, the pup was abandoned in freezing weather in South Korea. Plus, this was her fourth attempt to clinch the world’s ugliest title, and she finally made it after being first runner-up last year. Take that same energy to prepare for your next sales presentation.

item.title: Dairy Brew: Raw milk rebels and sixty dollar butter
item.description:
A splash of milk culture...
Good morning. Got milk? Because we sure do. Welcome to Dairy Brew, a special edition all about the business of the stuff that Joey from Friends claims he can drink a gallon of in 10 seconds . We’ll explain why some Americans swear by raw milk despite the health risks, discuss whether soy, coconut, and other plant-based “milks” really count as milk, look into why celebs are lathering dairy products all over their bodies, and a lot more.
